cli.browser_node.heading_dry_run: Node browser on {node} — dry run, nothing was changed:
cli.browser_node.heading_uninstall_dry_r: Removing the node browser from {node} — dry run, nothing was changed:
cli.browser_node.step_skipped: {step}: skipped, because an earlier step failed
cli.browser_node.refuse_platform: Refused: the node-managed browser supports Linux on x86_64 only; this is {system} {machine}.
cli.browser_node.refuse_distro: Refused: the node-managed browser needs a dnf/rpm distribution (Amazon Linux 2023, Fedora or the RHEL family).
cli.browser_node.refuse_user_machine: Refused: this is a user's machine ({reason}). On a user's machine the browser tool drives that person's own Chrome through the extension or the desktop app — see guide://browser.
cli.browser_node.refuse_not_member: Refused: this device is not in a lop mesh network. Join one first (guide://network), then run this again.
cli.browser_node.refuse_sudo: Refused: these steps need root and `sudo -n` would prompt: {steps}. Run it from an account with non-interactive sudo, or have an administrator apply those steps (guide://browser, "Headless nodes").
cli.browser_node.refuse_no_record: Refused: there is nothing to repair, because {path} does not exist. Install it with `lop browser setup --node --authorised-by '<who>'`.
cli.browser_node.refuse_authorisation: Refused: installing a browser on a node needs the operator's authorisation. Run it again with --authorised-by '<who authorised it, and when>'; the text is recorded verbatim.
cli.browser_node.paired_yes: Paired: yes. New sessions on this node get the browser tool; sessions that were already running do not.
cli.browser_node.failed_tail: Setup stopped at the failed step. Fix it, then run `lop browser setup --node --repair --authorised-by '<who>'`.
cli.browser_node.help_setup: Set up the node-managed browser on a headless mesh node
cli.browser_node.help_node: Install the node-managed headless Chrome (headless mesh nodes only)
cli.browser_node.help_dry_run: Show every step and whether it is already in place; change nothing
cli.browser_node.help_repair: Re-apply only the steps that are no longer in place on an existing install
cli.browser_node.help_upgrade: Move the pinned Chrome and the extension to their newest verified versions
cli.browser_node.help_extension_dir: Pack this built extension directory instead of the newest GitHub Release asset
cli.browser_node.help_authorised_by: Who authorised this, and when; recorded verbatim (required unless --dry-run)
cli.browser_node.help_uninstall_node: Remove the node-managed browser (unit, policy, version lock, Chrome package)
